title: Best Dehumidifier for a Two-Story House & Upstairs (2026)
h1: The Best Dehumidifiers for a Two-Story House, Upstairs and Down
dek: Two floors usually means two different humidity problems. Here's how to cover both without hauling a full bucket up the stairs.
description: The best dehumidifier for a two-story house, from upstairs and second-floor picks to pump units for the lowest level, plus exactly where to put each one.
intro: Choosing a **dehumidifier for a two-story house** starts with an awkward truth: one portable unit rarely fixes both floors. Moisture collects at the bottom of a home, in basements and slab-level rooms, while upstairs dampness usually comes from showers, an attic or an air conditioner that cools without drying. For most homes, the best first move is a capable unit on the lowest level, and our top pick for that job is the **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump**, which drains itself so nobody carries water up the stairs.

This guide is for owners of two-story and split-level homes who want to know what to buy and where to put it. The three decisions that matter most are which floor actually needs help (measure before you buy), how each unit will drain on a floor with no floor drain, and whether you'd be better served by one ducted system that treats the whole house. Upstairs, a compact, quiet unit like the **Midea Cube 20** usually does the job in the rooms that need it.
topPicksLead: The **Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump** is our top pick for a two-story house because it handles the dampest, lowest floor and drains itself.

products.notes: Run it with the basement door closed for the first week to bring that level under control, then open it up.

Quieter bedroom choices are in our [best dehumidifier for bedroom](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-bedroom/) guide.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifiers for two-story houses

blocks.text: We don't lab-test. We compare DOE 2019 and AHAM capacity ratings, ENERGY STAR listings, owner's manuals and CPSC recall records, then read owner reviews for the things that matter in a multi-level home: how heavy the tank is to carry, how well pumps and hoses work without a floor drain, and whether app readings are reliable enough to check one floor from another. Every pick is a verified Amazon listing.

sections.heading: How to choose a dehumidifier for a two-story home

items.label: Measure each floor first
items.text: Put an inexpensive [hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/) on each level for a few days. Anything consistently above 55–60% needs help; a floor that sits at 45% doesn't.

items.label: Size by floor, not by house
items.text: A 2,400 sq ft two-story home is really two 1,200 sq ft spaces separated by a stairwell. Size each unit for the floor or room it serves using our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: Solve upstairs drainage
items.text: Second floors almost never have floor drains.
sub: Unit higher than a tub or shower drain: gravity hose
Drain is higher or far away: built-in pump
Small room you visit daily: a lift-out tank

items.label: Mind the weight on stairs
items.text: A full 2–4 gallon tank weighs roughly 17–35 pounds. On a lower level, a pump or hose takes stairs out of the routine entirely.

items.label: Keep noise away from bedrooms
items.text: Upstairs units often run near sleeping areas. Choose a compact unit with a humidistat, so it cycles off rather than droning all night.

items.label: Consider one ducted system
items.text: If both floors are humid and you have forced-air HVAC, a whole-house unit can cost less to live with than two or three portables.

sections.heading: Upstairs or downstairs? Where to put a dehumidifier in a 2-story house

blocks.text: In most homes, start downstairs. The lowest level sits against cool soil, so it has the highest relative humidity and the musty smells that drift up through the house. Treat that floor first, then measure upstairs again before buying anything else.
Will a dehumidifier in the basement help upstairs?

A little, but less than people hope. Moisture does spread between floors, and drying the basement removes a major source, so upstairs often improves slightly. But a portable unit mostly dries the air around it, and a closed door or a narrow stairwell limits how much air it ever sees from the second floor. If upstairs is still above 55% after the basement is under control, it needs its own unit or a ducted system.

blocks.title: Why upstairs can read drier
blocks.text: Warm air holds more moisture, so a second floor that runs a few degrees warmer can show lower relative humidity even when the moisture content is the same. That's one more reason to measure before you buy. Our [placement guide](/guides/where-to-place-a-dehumidifier/) covers clearance and spot-by-spot tips.

sections.heading: Why is my upstairs so humid?

items: **Showers without a working exhaust fan.** Upstairs bathrooms are the biggest daily moisture source on most second floors.
**An oversized air conditioner.** A system that cools fast and shuts off before it has removed much moisture leaves rooms cool but clammy.

**Attic heat and leaks.** A hot, poorly vented attic or a small roof leak can raise humidity in the rooms below; our [attic dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-attic/) guide covers the space itself.
**One thermostat for two floors.** When the thermostat lives downstairs, the second floor often gets less conditioning time and stays muggier.
**Damp basement, no floor drain:** the Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump.
**Damp basement with a floor drain, on a budget:** the Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1.
**One or two muggy upstairs bedrooms:** a Midea Cube 20 in each room that needs it.
**A humid bonus room, loft or room over the garage:** the Honeywell TP30AWKN.
**Both floors humid, forced-air HVAC:** the Aprilaire E100, installed by a pro. Compare more systems in our [whole-house dehumidifier](/best/best-whole-house-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: In a two-story house, start at the bottom: a 50-pint unit with a pump, like the Midea 50-Pint Smart with Pump, fixes the floor where moisture collects and spares you trips up the stairs with a full bucket. Then measure the second floor and add a compact unit only to the rooms that need it. If every floor stays clammy all summer, one ducted Aprilaire E100 is the cleaner long-term fix.

faqs.q: Should a dehumidifier go upstairs or downstairs?
faqs.a: Downstairs first in most homes, because the lowest level is usually the dampest. Once it's under control, check upstairs with a hygrometer; if it's still above about 55%, add a unit to the rooms that need it.

faqs.q: Will a dehumidifier in the basement help upstairs?
faqs.a: Somewhat. Drying the basement removes a major moisture source, but a portable unit mainly dries the air around it. A closed door or narrow stairwell limits its reach, so a humid second floor usually needs its own unit or a ducted system.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a second floor?
faqs.a: For a single bedroom or office, 20–22 pints is enough. For a bonus room, loft or open upstairs living area, step up to about 30–35 pints. Treating an entire humid second floor is a job for a 50-pint unit in a central hallway or a ducted system.

faqs.q: Can one dehumidifier work for a whole two-story house?
faqs.a: A single portable rarely can, because floors and doors break up the airflow. A ducted whole-house dehumidifier such as the Aprilaire E100 can, since it uses your HVAC vents to reach every floor.

faqs.q: How do I drain a dehumidifier on the second floor?
faqs.a: If the unit sits higher than a tub or shower drain, run a gravity hose into it. Otherwise choose a model with a built-in pump that can push water up to a sink, or plan on emptying a tank you can carry level, like the Midea Cube 20's base reservoir.

faqs.q: What is the best place to put a dehumidifier in a 2-story house?
faqs.a: In the central, open part of the dampest floor, usually the basement or ground level, with about a foot of clearance around it and interior doors to that space closed while it works.
